prompt.context: Our client would like us to estimate the market for artificial turf.
prompt.question: How would you approach estimating the market size for artificial turf?

clarifying_info.q: What segments or uses of artificial turf should we focus on?
clarifying_info.a: This is a market sizing problem — you should lead the discussion and brainstorm the uses yourself. The interviewer will rarely provide additional information.

clarifying_info.q: Should we focus on a specific geography?

exhibits.title: Market Sizing Calculation Worksheet
exhibits.shows: A page with numerical calculations and assumptions used for estimating the artificial turf market in US schools
exhibits.data: Population 300M, age cohort 1%, high school attendance 80%, average class size 250, college attendance 25%, average graduating class 400, community college attendance 10%, average graduating class 200, turf price $10/sq ft, turf lifetime 10 years, field size 60yd x 120yd, adoption rate 50%

framework: Identify all major use segments for artificial turf (sports fields, commercial, residential, airports, schools)
Select a segment to size in depth — schools (high schools, colleges, community colleges)
Estimate number of institutions in each sub-segment using population-based build-up
Estimate sq footage of turf per institution (field dimensions × adoption rate)
Estimate annual replacement demand (total sq ft ÷ turf lifetime in years)
Multiply: number of schools × annual sq ft per school × price per sq ft = market size
Sanity-check the result and note assumptions

questions.prompt: Brainstorm the key uses / segments for artificial turf.
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover: sports fields (football, soccer, rugby, golf), commercial businesses, residential, airports, and schools (high schools, colleges, community colleges). Candidate should structure these clearly before diving into calculations.

questions.prompt: Estimate the number of high schools in the United States.
questions.guidance: Use a population build-up: total US population → fraction at age 18 → fraction attending high school → divide by average senior class size. Round sensibly.

math.setup: US population = 300M; 1% at age 18 = 3M; 80% attend high school = 2.4M; average 250 seniors per high school

questions.prompt: Estimate the number of 4-year colleges and community colleges in the United States.
questions.guidance: Apply the same age-cohort logic, using lower college-attendance rates and larger graduating class sizes for 4-year colleges, smaller for community colleges.

math.setup: People age 19 = 300M × 1% = 3M; 4-yr college attendance 25%; graduating class 400; community college attendance 10%; graduating class 200

questions.prompt: Calculate the total annual market size for artificial turf in US schools.
questions.guidance: Combine total number of schools, estimate sq ft of one athletic field, apply adoption rate, divide by turf lifetime to get annual demand, then multiply by price per sq ft.

math.setup: Total schools = 9,600 + 1,875 + 1,500 = 13,000 (≈13,000); field = 60yd × 120yd = 180ft × 360ft = 64,800 sq ft; adoption = 50%; lifetime = 10 years; price = $10/sq ft
steps: Annual sq ft per school = (1/10) × 50% × 64,800 = 3,240 sq ft

brainstorming.prompt: What are all the possible uses / segments for artificial turf?

recommendation: The US market for artificial turf in schools alone is approximately $420 million per year
The total market including commercial, residential, and other segments would be meaningfully larger
risks: Adoption rate assumption (50%) is uncertain and drives the result significantly
Turf lifetime of 10 years may vary widely by product quality and usage
Estimate excludes replacement driven by damage or upgrades, which could increase demand
next_steps: Extend the analysis to other segments (commercial, residential, airports) to size the full market
Validate adoption rate assumptions with industry data or client knowledge
Assess pricing trends — cost of artificial turf has fallen over time, affecting market value vs. volume
